title: Dhanvantari and the Three Doshas
word: the three doshas as a way of noticing
hookLine: a god rises from the churned ocean holding the drink of immortality, and a whole tradition of healing begins
carry: ayurveda, the knowledge of life, is a gift of god
tomorrow: why do some Hindu kitchens cook without onion or garlic?

lines: DHANTERAS: A LAMP BY THE DOOR.
cards: Two days before Diwali, many Hindu families buy something new for the house, a steel pot, a spoon, sometimes a little gold, and set a lamp by the door. The day is Dhanteras. Most people think of it as a day for wealth.
But it's also kept as the birthday of a god who walked out of the ocean holding a pot, and in that pot was the cure for death itself.
He's honored as the god of a whole tradition of medicine, and that's where this path turns now: Ayurveda, held here as a lens for noticing, never as a diagnosis.

teach.b: It's one of the great scenes in Hindu story. The gods and the asuras churn the ocean of milk for amrita, the drink of immortality.
Wonder after wonder rises out of the foam, and then a shining figure steps up carrying a pot: Dhanvantari, holding the amrita itself.
The Bhagavata Purana counts him among the forms of Vishnu, and Hindus honor him as the god of Ayurveda, a name that means the knowledge, veda, of life, ayus.
The Sushruta Samhita calls Ayurveda a branch of the Atharva Veda: the healing hymns of last week, grown up. On Dhanteras many families pray to Dhanvantari for health, beside Lakshmi for plenty.
So here's the teaching: in this tradition, caring for a body is holy work. Healing rose out of the same ocean as the gods' nectar. Ayurveda's first vocabulary is three words.

teach.h: VATA MOVES. PITTA HEATS. KAPHA HOLDS.
teach.b: The Ashtanga Hridaya, in paraphrase: wind, bile and phlegm; in brief, these are the three doshas, vata, pitta and kapha. Vata moves: breath, a darting thought. Pitta heats and changes: digestion, a flash of temper.
Kapha holds: weight, steadiness. All three are forces in every body, at once. Ayurveda has its own trained practitioners.

teach.h: A WAY OF NOTICING, NOT A DIAGNOSIS.
teach.b: On this path the doshas are held one way only, as a way of noticing, never a diagnosis; questions about your health belong with a doctor.

how: Hindus honor Dhanvantari as the god of Ayurveda and many pray to him for health on Dhanteras; Ayurveda is practiced by trained practitioners, and on this path the three doshas are used only as a vocabulary for noticing, never to diagnose or treat anything.

games.why: Dhanvantari, counted among Vishnu's forms, rose holding the amrita. Hindus honor him as the god of Ayurveda and pray to him for health.

practice: Find something moving: the breath, going in and out on its own. Then something warm, your palms or the air in your mouth, and something steady, the weight of your body on the seat.
Let all three be there at once, without deciding anything about them. If you pray, ask for health the way families do on Dhanteras, for yourself and for someone you love.

wordCard.voice: The three doshas, as a way of noticing, not a diagnosis. Vata, pitta, kapha: what moves, what heats, what holds.

orig.note: Sanskrit: one of the three forces of Ayurveda; the word can also mean a fault.

carryVoice: Your line: ayurveda, the knowledge of life, is a gift of god. Dhanvantari's pot, and three forces, never a verdict. That's today, done.
